title: 1499-dynamic-quantification-of-player-value
universal_lens: The H-scoring framework unifies dynamic roster valuation through a constrained optimization over category weights and positional allocations. By mapping player performance distributions to category win probabilities via error functions, it establishes a structural isomorphism between combinatorial lineup construction and continuous gradient-based value maximization.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the H-scoring objective to a hierarchical Bayesian model where category weights act as latent hyperparameters. Conformal inference bounds are applied to the multivariate normal X-score assumptions, quantifying epistemic uncertainty in weekly performance projections and dynamically adjusting draft valuations when empirical tail risks exceed nominal variance.
gse_mapping: GSE treats the snake draft as a Markov decision process. The assignment problem (Jonker-Volgenant) defines state transitions by optimally slotting drafted players into least-desirable positions. Gradient descent on V(j) computes the optimal policy, maximizing expected format wins against an evolving board of available assets.

primitives.name: Dynamic Value Optimization Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **H-scoring framework:** for each candidate player, (1) estimate optimal strategy parameters j maximizing a format objective V(j); (2) draft the player with highest V(j).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: j: dimensionless vector of category weights and flex-share allocations; V(j): dimensionless probability of winning the specified fantasy format objective.
primitives.assumptions: Format objective V(j) is differentiable with respect to strategy parameters j; future pick values follow a multivariate normal distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs at initialization v where gradients are undefined; fails if V(j) exhibits highly non-convex landscapes preventing local optima convergence.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's adaptive DFS budget allocation, replacing static ADP with real-time marginal value gradients.
layer2.telemetry: Win rate differential vs static G-score drafting across 1000 simulated seasons.

primitives.name: Differential Win Probability Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Three functions: X(j) = distribution of category-total differentials vs opponents; W(X(j)) = category win probabilities = CDF of the differential at zero; V(W) = format objective.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: X(j): dimensionless category-total differential; w_c: dimensionless probability of winning a specific category; \mu, \sigma: mean and standard deviation of the differential distribution.
primitives.assumptions: Category differentials X(j) are normally distributed; week-to-week category performances are independent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under heavy-tailed performance blocks where the normal CDF severely underestimates outlier probabilities.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction intervals, translating raw statistical edges into calibrated probabilistic win kernels.
layer2.telemetry: Calibration error between predicted w_c and empirical category win frequencies.

primitives.name: Optimal Slot Allocation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Positional model:** assignment problem (Jonker-Volgenant via scikit-learn) placing drafted players in least-desirable eligible slots, freeing good slots for future picks; flex shares control expected position mix.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Assignment cost matrix: dimensionless negative X-scores; Flex shares: dimensionless probabilities summing to 1 across eligible positions.
primitives.assumptions: Fixed positional structure; players can be assigned to any eligible slot without altering their underlying performance distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if positional scarcity creates discrete jumps in value not captured by continuous flex-share vectors.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSE lineup construction constraints, optimizing roster geometry to maximize future optionality.
layer2.telemetry: Variance reduction in projected roster totals post-assignment.

reasoning_traces.think:
The H-scoring primitive derives from the necessity to replace static Average Draft Position (ADP) heuristics with a dynamic, state-aware valuation kernel. Mathematically, it formulates the draft as a sequential optimization problem where the state is defined by the current roster and the remaining player pool. The core operator maximizes a format-specific objective function V(j), which is constructed hierarchically: first, player performances are normalized into X-scores, assuming a multivariate normal distribution. Second, these scores are aggregated into category differentials against simulated opponents. Third, the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of these differentials—specifically the error function—is evaluated at zero to yield category win probabilities w_c. Finally, these probabilities are combined into an overall format win probability V, such as the probability of winning the majority of categories. The dualities emerge in the treatment of positional scarcity; the Jonker-Volgenant algorithm solves an assignment problem that minimizes the opportunity cost of slotting a drafted player, effectively treating positional slots as a constrained resource. Failure modes are intrinsically tied to the Gaussian assumption. Real-world sports data exhibits heavy right tails and significant week-to-week correlations, meaning the normal CDF will miscalibrate extreme outlier events. Furthermore, the reliance on gradient descent guarantees only local optima, potentially trapping the drafter in suboptimal category-punting strategies if the initialization vector is poorly chosen.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits from classical portfolio theory, specifically the optimization of risk-adjusted returns, but transposes it into a combinatorial auction setting. It echoes the Kelly criterion in its focus on maximizing geometric growth of win probability rather than raw point totals. Historically, it bridges the gap between static scouting rankings and modern, simulation-heavy Monte Carlo draft assistants, formalizing intuitive value-based drafting into a rigorous, differentiable mathematical object.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The model explicitly incorporates a theory of mind regarding opposing agents by assuming they adhere to a static G-score ranking strategy. This simplification allows the H-scoring agent to predict the depletion curve of high-value assets with high confidence. However, this creates a brittle adversarial model; if opponents also adopt dynamic, adaptive strategies, the assumed availability of future picks collapses, leading to severe overvaluation of players targeted by multiple adaptive agents.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises from the assumption of week-to-week category independence. In reality, athletic outputs are highly correlated (e.g., rushing attempts and yards). Ignoring this covariance induces leakage between layers, causing the conformal bounds on category win probabilities to be overly narrow. Additionally, the equal-variance assumption acts as an anti-collinearity filter; if two players have identical means but vastly different volatilities, the model fails to distinguish their true optionality, necessitating a veto on homogeneous variance priors.
